what_its_for: Cabozantinib is a cancer medicine used to treat certain types of kidney cancer, liver cancer, and thyroid cancer. It works by blocking signals that help cancer cells grow and spread, and by cutting off the blood supply that tumors need to survive.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet or capsule whole with a full glass of water. Do NOT crush, chew, or break it. Take it on an empty stomach — do not eat for at least 1 hour before and at least 2 hours after taking your dose. Take it at the same time every day to help you remember. If you take Cometriq (capsules), do not open the capsules.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your type of cancer and overall health. Common doses are 20 mg, 40 mg, or 60 mg once daily. Always follow your doctor's instructions exactly. Do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and your next scheduled dose is more than 12 hours away, take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If your next dose is less than 12 hours away, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store cabozantinib at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Store it in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines safely out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about proper disposal.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating grapefruit or drinking grapefruit juice while taking this medicine, as it can raise the level of cabozantinib in your blood and increase side effects. Avoid St. John's Wort supplements, as they can make this medicine less effective. Avoid taking antacids, calcium supplements, or iron supplements within 2 hours of your dose. Tell your doctor before starting any new prescription, over-the-counter, or herbal medicines. Avoid getting pregnant — use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 4 months after your last dose.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: severe stomach pain, vomiting blood, or black/tarry stools (signs of bleeding); sudden severe headache, chest pain, or difficulty breathing; numbness, tingling, or pain in your hands or feet; jaw pain or swelling; wounds that are not healing; high blood pressure that is hard to control; signs of a blood clot such as leg swelling, redness, or warmth; severe diarrhea that will not stop; skin sores on your hands or feet (hand-foot syndrome); signs of liver problems like yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or unusual tiredness; or any new or worsening symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: Cabozantinib does not cure cancer, but it can slow the growth and spread of cancer cells. Most people do not feel the medicine working right away. Your doctor will check on how well the medicine is working through regular scans and blood tests, usually after several weeks to months of treatment. Keep taking it as directed, even if you feel well.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Do NOT take this medicine if you are pregnant, as it can harm your unborn baby. Do not breastfeed while taking cabozantinib and for at least 4 months after your last dose. Seniors: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects — your doctor will monitor you closely. Liver problems: If you have moderate to severe liver disease, your dose may need to be adjusted. Kidney problems: No dose adjustment is usually needed for mild to moderate kidney problems, but tell your doctor about any kidney issues. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in children for most conditions.
